note: What hunts you in water, where none of the answers that work on land do: you cannot climb, you cannot outrun what swims, and a boat is only a place to be caught standing. The last two of the four never see open sea — they are what is waiting in a drowned hold, and a shark is the one thing that is in both places. Fields are as described in beasts.json.

shark.note: It circles before it commits, which is the only warning water ever gives. Two damage a pass against a hero who cannot back away is what makes swimming a decision.
shark.label: Shark

orca.note: The shark's argument, larger: quicker than anything in the water, hitting for three, and worth a small fortune to anybody mad enough to be in the sea with a blade.
orca.label: Orca

squid.note: The slow half of a drowned hold. It does not chase — it does not have to, in a room you have to wade across — and what it costs you is the time you spend getting past it, which is time the fish-folk are using. Hits harder than anything else this shallow.
squid.label: Squid
lines: *an arm comes out of the dark*

fishfolk.note: Whatever was aboard when she went down, or whatever moved in afterwards — the game does not say, and the villagers have four stories about it. They come in twos and threes and they use a room: the point of a drowned hold is that it is a fight you cannot back out of a doorway from, because the doorway is underwater too.
fishfolk.label: Fish-folk
